name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
title: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
answer: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the use of software rules to hold, release, and reconcile funds between parties in payables and receivables. It applies to milestone payments, trade finance, marketplace payouts, subscription billing, and any transaction where payment depends on a verified event or document. The scope includes the design of conditional logic, the custody of escrowed balances, and the accounting entries that follow each release. It also covers the interfaces between settlement systems and the ledgers, invoices, and contracts that define the obligation.

sections.body: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the use of software rules to hold, release, and reconcile funds between parties in payables and receivables. It applies to milestone payments, trade finance, marketplace payouts, subscription billing, and any transaction where payment depends on a verified event or document. The scope includes the design of conditional logic, the custody of escrowed balances, and the accounting entries that follow each release. It also covers the interfaces between settlement systems and the ledgers, invoices, and contracts that define the obligation.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems run on a mix of conventional payment rails and programmatic layers. A typical stack includes an ERP or accounting system, a payment API or treasury platform, a database or distributed ledger that records conditions and state, and identity or approval services. Some implementations use public blockchains and stablecoins, while others use permissioned ledgers or ordinary databases with strong audit logs. Connectivity to bank accounts, card networks, and real-time payment schemes is usually required for the final movement of money.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins by translating a contract or purchase order into machine-readable conditions, such as delivery confirmation, inspection sign-off, or invoice matching. Funds are then committed to an escrow account or a smart contract, and release is triggered by an authorized event, an oracle feed, or a human approval. AI can assist by extracting terms from documents, matching invoices to receipts, and flagging exceptions before settlement. Reconciliation, audit trails, and exception handling are built into the workflow so that every release maps to a payable or receivable entry.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risks turn on legal enforceability, custody, and evidence. A programmable escrow must respect money transmission rules, sanctions screening, anti-money laundering checks, and the accounting standards that apply to the parties. Code errors, oracle failures, and disputed conditions can delay or misdirect funds, so version control, access controls, and independent review matter. Provenance is maintained through immutable or tamper-evident logs that record who authorized each step, what condition was met, and which version of the rules was in force.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward tighter integration between programmable logic and regulated payment systems. Expect more use of tokenized deposits, real-time settlement networks, and standardized payment messages that carry condition data alongside the payment. AI agents may increasingly negotiate terms and initiate settlements within pre-approved limits, with humans handling exceptions. The pace will depend on clearer legal treatment of smart contracts, consistent accounting guidance, and the willingness of banks and corporates to connect their ledgers to shared settlement infrastructure.
